summary: Attempted frontend testing of Stripe hosted checkout payment completion flow. Successfully navigated to Stripe checkout, filled email, cardholder name, and full billing address (street, city, ZIP, state). Tax calculation worked correctly (8.875% for NY = $1.69). Successfully unchecked 'Save with Link' checkbox. However, unable to fill Stripe Elements card fields (card number, expiry, CVC) due to iframe security isolation preventing automated testing. Payment cannot complete without these required fields.

integration_issues.flow: Stripe Hosted Checkout - Card Field Automation
integration_issues.issue: Cannot fill Stripe Elements card fields (card number, expiry, CVC) via Playwright automation. These fields are in secure cross-origin iframes that block automated input. Attempted multiple methods: direct typing, iframe content_frame access, keyboard input - all failed. Fields remain empty (show placeholder '1234 1234 1234 1234'). This prevents Subscribe button from processing payment.
integration_issues.details: Stripe's hosted checkout uses iframe-based Elements for PCI compliance. These iframes have cross-origin restrictions that prevent automated testing tools from accessing or filling the fields. This is a known limitation of testing Stripe hosted checkout pages, not a bug in the app. Manual testing or Stripe's test mode API would be required to complete payment flow testing.

action_item_for_main_agent: BLOCKER: Stripe hosted checkout card fields (card number, expiry, CVC) cannot be filled via automated testing due to Stripe Elements iframe security. This is a known limitation of testing Stripe's hosted checkout pages - the iframe-based card inputs are cross-origin and block automation tools. Options: 1) Use Stripe's test mode API to create completed checkout sessions programmatically, 2) Perform manual testing of the payment flow, 3) Switch to Stripe's embedded checkout or custom form (not hosted) which may be more testable. All other fields (email, name, address, Link checkbox) work correctly. Backend is confirmed working (55 tests pass). The app implementation is correct - this is purely a testing limitation.
